root.name: Rubinstein Opening: Classical Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. Nf3 e6 3. e3 c5 4. Bd3 d5 5. b3 Nc6 6. O-O Be7 7. Bb2 O-O

overview: A Colle-Zukertort style set-up against Black's ...c5/...d5/...Nc6 formation: White has e3, Bd3, b3, Bb2 and castled, Black mirrors with ...Be7 and ...O-O. The centre stays in tension (dxc5 or c4 later), and the game is a manoeuvring fight over d4/d5 and the e-file with no immediate tactics.

white_ideas.idea: Hold d4 and aim Bb2/Bd3 at the kingside
Play c4 or dxc5 at the right moment to open the position
Bring the knight to e5 via Nbd2

black_ideas.idea: Keep a hanging-pawn or symmetrical centre

typical_structures.structure: Symmetrical d4/e3 against d5/e6 with c5 pawn tension
Hanging pawns on c5/d5 after exchanges

character.notes: Quiet development on both sides, tension in the centre but nothing forcing yet.

structure.notes: The d4/c5/d5 pawns are in contact but undecided, so the centre stays flexible.

approach.notes: A specific set-up against ...Nf6, ...e6, ...c5, ...d5 rather than a universal system.

level.notes: Plans are clear but choosing between dxc5, c4 and e4 breaks needs judgement.

plan_phrases: Bishop on b2 aimed at the kingside

character.reason: Quiet development with the centre in tension but no forcing play.
